method: TRUNCATION ORACLE: for each sampled as-of day t the engine view build(bars, {asOf: t}) is compared with build(bars <= t, evidence truncated outside the engine by its own publication timestamp, no asOf). Any difference in segments, holds, invalid ranges, normalizations or a total-return ratio (1e-9) is a violation. Timestamps: every SEC observation is compared with its EDGAR acceptance time (data.sec.gov/submissions, a different SEC system than the full-text search that supplies visibleAt); an observation treated as public before its acceptance day (US/Eastern) is a violation. observedAt of every hold, normalization, invalid range and RESUME_FROM must appear in the oracle view of that day (else OBSERVED_AT_TOO_EARLY, a violation); appearing already one session earlier is reported as late (conservative, not a violation). Revisions at +1/+5/+20 sessions and lag distributions are disclosed (review R2-07).
independence: independent of the engine's as-of filtering (inputs physically truncated) and of the EFTS extraction (acceptance times from the submissions index). The SEC remains the authority for its own publication time; FINRA has a single timestamp (dailyListDatetime), so FINRA timing is checked by truncation only (disclosed limit). The signature/tr comparison re-runs the truncation outside the engine and is reported as a consistency check; the independent parts are the acceptance-time comparison (decision observations) and the observedAt-in-oracle-view check (review P3-06).

finding: 2 SEC observations carry an EFTS filing date before their EDGAR acceptance day (US/Eastern). None is behind a decision, but an as-of view on the acceptance day could see them: the evidence model must take visibleAt = max(filing date, acceptance day) - a rule change for the next protocol, not applied here.
